Twenty-nine comments

I don’t have a name for this tune but heard it on a Stockton’s Wing album - I think the track name is The Golden Stud. The track begins with Maurice Lennon playing The Unfortunate Rake, followed by a spoken vocal merging into this tune. I’m not even certain it is a hornpipe. Does anyone know more about this one ? I searched the database and googled The Golden Stud but didn’t get any more info. I also searched with various bars in ABC which didn’t give any results either.

↳ Posted by stoneboy on July 16th, 2005.

Golden Stud

The title of the tune is indeed “The Golden Stud”, and I think is more a slowish reel than hornpipe. It was composed by either Maurice Lennon or Paul Roche [ not sure which ], in the early days of “Stockton’s Wing” , and the name referred to somebody’s ear-ring. This used to be the track where Steve Cooney played didgeridoo, starting with the jig you mention, going into this tune, and finishing with “The Morning Dew”. Clever stuff, and this tune still occasionally turns up in sessions.

↳ Posted by nfritzjr on June 29th, 2012.

Very probably, Nick….

I haven’t heard the “Live” album, but have heard them play it live, if you know what I mean. [ Edinburgh, 1982 ]. The set began with a jig called, among other things, “Up Sligo” - “The Golden Stud” is the middle tune, and the set ends with “The Morning Dew”.
The set was also on the “Light In The Northern Sky” album, but there is no clue anywhere on the album, insert or sleeve notes as to who wrote it. If I come across Kieran Hanrahan at the Willie Week in 10 days time, I’ll ask him, to settle this once and for all.

The Golden Stud, X:15

For this one, I’ve fused what I’ve heard in my local sessions with how “The Golden Stud” is usually played in a couple Irish music festivals that took place in France.
The 2nd, 6th and 11th settings on this page are frequently used as variations during repeats.
Bar 4 can be played identical to bar 8 if your instrument doesn’t allow you to play it as written.
